For Quinn Slack, Amp’s CEO, each improvement in the models is an opportunity to expand what the agent can do, from helping developers decide what to build to writing code and designing pages.
L45: Amp chooses and recommends models based on what works best for its users, and OpenAI models account for the majority of tokens used in Amp. Quinn shares, “OpenAI is very transparent, and when there are safeguards applied, users know and they understand. That makes it really easy to use OpenAI models. You can do all of your work in Amp with OpenAI models and be really happy.”
L46: 
L47: > “Our users really appreciate the consistency with which OpenAI models have been getting better and better.”
L48: —Quinn Slack, CEO and member of technical staff, Amp
L49: ## Lowering the cost of building with Sign in with ChatGPT
L50: 
L51: As builders give agents more work, token costs can become a constraint. Quinn describes some Amp users consuming 10 billion tokens a week. He believes that if people watch every increment of usage, it might hold them back from finding out what an agent is capable of.
L52: To help alleviate that, Amp launched its Sign in with ChatGPT integration. Quinn says it gives Amp users access to more tokens and OpenAI models, including GPT‑6 Astra, which changes how willing they are to let an agent take on a larger task.
L53: “Sign in with ChatGPT means that people can have that feeling where they’re not counting every single token,” he says. “And once you actually let the agent go and have a longer leash, then you realize just how much it can do.” Quinn says he sees people using the agent to plan, decide what to build, and continue working after they ship.
L54: ## Writing, designing, and creating with GPT‑6 Astra
L55: 
L56: Amp wants agents to help with all the work that goes into building and growing a product. Its own 20-person team uses them that way, including in marketing. “We don’t have someone devoted to it, but we have an agent devoted to it,” Quinn says. The team relies on the agent to improve the experience for new users and help more people discover Amp through search and other channels.
L57: For that work, having high-quality writing and design is critical. GPT‑6 Astra helps the team produce documentation and design pages that meet Amp’s exacting standards.
L58: 
L59: > “We have a very unique design style and writing style. We’re very picky about this, but we’ve been really happy with how GPT-6 Astra does.”
L60: 
L61: —Quinn Slack, CEO and member of technical staff, Amp
L62: Quinn’s experiments with GPT‑6 Astra continue at home. He gave it the plans for his house and used it to create a 3D model in Blender. He and his children then turn that model into games: adding a lazy river through the house or chasing garlic around it, inspired by their grandmother’s dislike of garlic. “And that was not possible just a couple months ago,” he says.
L63: ## Talking to your agent through GPT‑Live‑1
L64: 
L65: Amp recently announced Puck, a conversational AI assistant built into Amp that helps users launch and manage other agents. Users can ask Puck to start an agent to investigate a bug, coordinate several agents, or find a previous conversation about a technical problem.
L66: With Calling Puck, powered by GPT‑Live‑1, users can talk to Puck in real time, including from a watch. Quinn imagines people using it to keep their agents working while they’re away from their computers, even while out for a run.
L67: ## Accelerating agent workflows with Ultrafast
L68: 
L69: Amp has been testing Ultrafast mode with GPT‑6 Astra, and Quinn says the greater speed changes how people use agents. Today, people often switch between several agent tasks while waiting for each to finish. Faster responses could let people juggle fewer agents, or give agents more time to check their own work before returning a result.
L70: 
L71: > “People have not seen a model that’s this good, that’s this fast.”
L72: 
L73: —Quinn Slack, CEO and member of technical staff, Amp
L74: For Amp, the next step is to bring more of the work before and after coding into the agent, so builders can carry an idea further without handling every step themselves. “There’s this unknown of what humans will create, and that’s what we all get to see. It’s cool to be playing a part in that,” Quinn says.

articles.title: 【钛晨报】中国最新金融数据出炉，债券和股票融资在社融增量中占比近半；含DeepSeek、微信等，151款应用拒绝接入豆包手机助手；恒生指数公司出手，茶百道遭多个指数剔除
articles.text:
（本文作者为 钛媒体官方账号，钛媒体经授权发布）
【钛媒体综合】10月14日，中国人民银行发布前三季度金融数据，呈现诸多亮点。
初步统计，2026年前三季度社会融资规模增量累计为27.46万亿元，比上年同期少2.63万亿元。其中，企业债券净融资2.75万亿元，同比多1.18万亿元，企业债券在社会融资规模增量中的占比为10.01%；政府债券净融资10.3万亿元，同比少1.16万亿元；非金融企业境内股票融资5359亿元，同比多2191亿元。
根据测算，债券和股票融资在社会融资规模增量中的占比约49.48%，超过贷款占比约7个百分点，直接融资对信贷的替代效应进一步显现。特别是企业债券快速增长，9月末余额同比增长9.3%。
前三季度人民币贷款增加11.52万亿元。信贷资金主要流向了哪里？数据显示，企业端仍是主力，前三季度企（事）业单位贷款增加12.55万亿元，其中中长期贷款增加6.53万亿元，构成了企业信贷的“半壁江山”。居民端去杠杆态势延续，前三季度住户贷款减少1.03万亿元，2025年同期为增加1.1万亿元。
货币供应情况方面，9月末，广义货币（M2）余额为359.63万亿元，同比增长7.2%，涨幅较上月末小幅回落0.3个百分点。狭义货币（M1）余额116.76万亿元，同比增长3.2%，涨幅较上月末回落0.9个百分点。
东方金诚首席宏观分析师王青介绍，当前M2增速仍然明显高于名义GDP增速，显示货币政策保持支持性立场。M1增速出现放缓，除上年同期基数偏高，也可能与房地产市场持续调整，以及企业和居民投资、消费动能有待进一步提振等因素有关。中国民生银行首席经济学家温彬指出，去年9月M1出现超季节性增长，增速高达7.2%，使得今年同期M1增速在较高基数上回落较大。与此同时资本市场波动、机构调仓，非银存款再次出现阶段性收缩，这些因素也制约了M1、M2增速。
“目前我国社会融资规模、M2增速仍有7%以上，呈现中高速增长。”北京大学光华管理学院院长田轩表示，从中长期时间看，延续合理增长态势，“与经济增长、价格总水平预期目标相匹配”。
钛媒摘声：
AI失控是确定性事件，依据有四条：大模型已经升格为有手有脚、能操纵物理世界生产线的智能体；以Anthropic的Mythos为代表的AI已经能自动挖掘漏洞，而且挖得比人快、比人强；黑客攻击经验蒸馏进智能体之后，“100分的人类黑客很罕见，80分的AI黑客一口气可以复制1000个，不眠不休”；再叠加RSI带来的自我进化，“人类为什么永远无法消灭病毒？因为这玩意儿能进化，现在轮到AI能自我进化了”。
——360集团创始人周鸿祎
当前A股的国内流动性依然低迷，但AI仍是杠铃配置中增长端的核心主线。在当前市场风格下，继续看好杠铃策略，防御端配置高股息标的，增长端配置AI基础设施和CXO/创新药等增长主题。至于AI板块，地缘政治担忧的确压制AI板块估值，但估值合理的AI子板块可缓冲下行风险：存储和服务器/交换机ODM/OEM这两个垂直领域，未来12个月市销率合理且未来12个月销售同比增速可观。
——摩根大通中国股票策略师 张晓宁
国内公司：
含DeepSeek、微信等，151款应用拒绝接入豆包手机助手
10月14日，据豆包手机助手官方发布的内容显示，《屏幕自动化操作声明协议》30天公示期结束后，将逐步开放第三方应用的GUI自动化操作能力，开放范围限于未声明拒绝的应用。公示期结束后，开发者仍可声明拒绝。对于声明拒绝的应用，豆包手机助手不会进行相关操作。豆包同步对外披露了一份拒绝操作清单，共计151款应用不允许豆包手机助手对其执行GUI屏幕自动化操作，微信、DeepSeek、淘宝、快手、美团等大众高频应用尽数在列。
恒生指数公司出手，茶百道遭多个指数剔除
10月14日，恒生指数公司发布公告称，茶百道于香港联合交易所上市之股份受监管机构调查而停牌，其公司股份将会从恒生指数系列中剔除。茶百道将于2026年10月22日（星期四）开市前调整为系统最低价格（即0.0001港元）并用作当天指数计算，并于当天收市后以0.0001港元从下列指数中剔除，下述变动将于2026年10月23日（星期五）起生效。
周生生回应香港门店发生“珠宝大劫案”：已交由警方处理
据报道，10月14日下午3时许，香港大埔广福道70号一间周生生金行发生财物被抢案件。针对上述事件，周生生方面当日晚间表示，已交由警方处理，暂无其他信息。
嘉元科技：预计前三季度净利同比增长1197%-1319%，铜箔产销量显著增长
10月14日，嘉元科技公告称，预计2026年前三季度归属于母公司所有者的净利润为5.30亿元-5.80亿元，同比增长1197%-1319%。报告期内，下游行业景气度持续上升，拉动铜箔市场需求稳步增长，公司积极把握市场机遇，凭借优质的产品和深厚的客户积累，实现了铜箔产品产销量的显著增长，通过产能建设与技术改造提高产能，并推动公司产能利用率同比上升，单位生产成本降低，进而实现利润提升。同时，公司持续优化产品结构，提升高附加值产品销售占比，持续提高公司盈利能力。此外，公司始终坚持技术创新理念，持续优化生产工艺，有效提升产品品质，深化降本增效工作，对公司净利润产生积极影响。报告期内，公司非经常性损益较上年同期大幅增加，主要系公司公允价值变动收益和投资收益增加所致。
台积电有望提前完成明年产能目标
10月14日，据悉，由于市场对台积电2纳米工艺的需求十分旺盛，该公司有望提前完成2027年的生产目标。2纳米制程技术是台积电目前量产的最先进的制造技术，也是高性能人工智能芯片需要的成熟工艺。台积电此前的产能估计到2026年底最高约为每月10万片晶圆，但有报道指出，最新的估计将产量提高了20%，达到每月12万片晶圆。
宝能集团及姚振华等被执行20.5亿
天眼查显示，近日，深圳市宝能投资集团有限公司及其法定代表人姚振华等新增一则被执行人信息，执行标的20.5亿元人民币，执行法院为江西省南昌市中级人民法院。该公司成立于2000年3月，注册资本约3亿人民币，经营范围包括投资兴办实业，投资文化旅游产业，建筑、装饰材料的购销及其它国内贸易等，由姚振华、深圳赛康资产管理有限公司共同持股。
东百集团：终止收购杭州快灵光电部分股权
10月14日，东百集团公告称，公司全资子公司福建东百创智投资有限公司原拟收购杭州快灵光电科技有限公司部分股权，因各方未能就关键条款达成一致，公司决定终止本次股权收购。本次交易未签订正式协议，终止不会对公司财务状况和经营产生重大影响。
富祥股份：控股股东、实控人、董事长包建华被留置
富祥股份公告称，公司于2026年10月14日收到监察机关通知，控股股东、实际控制人、董事长包建华被留置。经初步了解，本次立案调查系包建华个人事项，与公司无关。公司拥有完善的组织架构和规范的治理体系，其他董事和高级管理人员均正常履职，生产经营情况正常，上述事项不会对公司生产经营产生重大影响。
国外企业：
发布700余篇AI数学手稿，OpenAI宣称攻克数百未解数学难题
OpenAI近日发布700多篇由其内部模型生成的数学手稿，声称其模型能够解决上百个数学难题，此举在学界引发争议。OpenAI声称，这些手稿解决了300多道人类之前无法攻克的数学难题，覆盖代数、逻辑、几何、概率等领域。这一事件引发广泛关注，促使数学家思考人工智能将如何冲击、重塑数学研究。法国数学家塞德里克·维拉尼直言，这将是数学领域的一场变革。不过，有不少数学家对OpenAI宣称的成果持怀疑态度。
苹果iPhone Duo完成大模型备案，Apple智能、通义千问等现身
工信部电信设备进网许可信息显示，苹果iPhone Duo折叠屏手机国行版（型号A3721）在今年9月2日获得试用批文许可证后，于9月29日完成换证，新增了所搭载大模型的备案编号。该设备搭载的大模型备案编号为：Shanghai-AppleZhiNeng-202506160057、Shanghai-TongYiWanXiang-202410090024、ZheJiang-TongYiQianWen-20230901，分别对应Apple智能、通义万象、通义千问。
光刻巨头CEO：订单已经谈到2030年
据披露，2026年第三季度，ASML实现净销售额117亿欧元，毛利率为57.5%，净利润达50亿欧元。ASML预计2026年第四季度净销售额在142亿欧元至152亿欧元之间，毛利率约为57%；预计2026年全年净销售额将介于440亿欧元至450亿欧元，毛利率约为56%。“第三季度净销售额接近此前预测区间的高位。客户持续上调对ASML设备的短期和中期需求预期，主要基于其对人工智能相关投资规模及持续周期的判断。目前，客户对未来市场需求前景更加清晰，并预计至少到2028年，行业仍将处于供不应求的状态。部分客户已与我们开始了2029年甚至2030年的设备订单接洽。”ASML总裁兼首席执行官表示。
Netflix据悉将全球裁员近6%，涉及产品、技术等部门
10月14日，据报道，Netflix将裁员近6%，涉及全球约1000个职位，为该公司2022年以来规模最大的一轮裁员，旨在应对增长放缓和用户参与度下滑等挑战。Netflix联席首席执行官Greg Peters和Ted Sarandos在致员工的电子邮件中表示，此次裁员主要涉及产品、技术、法务和人力资源部门。
ABB机器人中国区总裁：软银收购仍在推进，对中国市场承诺不变
针对软银集团收购ABB机器人的交易进展，ABB机器人中国区总裁韩晨在日前举行的工博会期间表示，“综合各方面反馈，整体进展向好，各项流程都在正常推进。”双方去年宣布该交易预计于2026年中后期完成，如今时间表已过大半，韩晨称“项目仍处于预设时间窗口之内。”韩晨强调，与软银的交易不会影响ABB机器人的在华策略。“中国作为全球规模最大的机器人市场，绝大多数机器人生产企业与系统集成供应商汇聚于此。无论股权归属如何，我们对中国市场的各项承诺不会动摇，国产化程度还将进一步深化。”
政策风向：
央行：10月15日开展7000亿元期限为6个月的买断式逆回购操作
央行公告，为保持银行体系流动性充裕，2026年10月15日，中国人民银行将以固定数量、利率招标、多重价位中标方式开展7000亿元买断式逆回购操作，期限为6个月（182天），到期日为2027年4月15日（遇节假日顺延）。
中小银行收债券投资提示？知情人士：并非全国统一安排
10月14日，有市场消息称，部分省份中小银行收到监管提示，要求金融投资增速不得高于贷款增速、新增债券久期不得高于存量久期。对此，知情人士表示，金融管理部门并未就中小银行金融投资增速和新增债券久期作出全国统一安排。在市场化原则下，中小银行基于自身资产负债状况进行的债券投资决策，属于其自主经营权范畴。不过，“自主经营权”与“制度约束”并行不悖。另一位知情人士称，商业银行利率风险水平和风险管理状况是受到明确制度约束的，地方监管部门将对辖内机构进行日常风险监测与提示，属于常规监管动作。
股市行情：
今年外资抛售三星电子、SK海力士合计176万亿韩元
10月14日，券商研报称，外国投资者持续抛售韩国股票，抛售态势暂未见缓解。但本月末至11月中旬的一系列事件，或将成为外资回流的转折点。两大存储芯片巨头财报、美国中期选举、中东局势变化、AI企业Anthropic上市，被视作有可能扭转市场情绪的核心变量。韩国交易所14日数据显示，截至前一交易日，外国投资者今年在韩国综合指数主板市场累计净卖出203.6977万亿韩元（约合1415亿美元）。其中仅三星电子、SK海力士两只股票就遭到净卖出约176万亿韩元，占外资总抛售规模的86%。三星电子外资持股比例降至2008年以来18年新低；SK海力士外资持股率也跌破十年均值。本轮外资撤离是KOSPI指数下行的核心推手。中东地缘风险加剧、OpenAI年度营收争议、以及外国企业竞争力提升带来的担忧，多重因素叠加压制市场。
慈文传媒：微短剧《开标之战》投资规模较小，目前归属于公司收入约50万元
10月14日，慈文传媒公告，公司股票连续二个交易日（2026年10月13日、10月14日）收盘价格涨幅偏离值累计超过20%，属于股票交易异常波动情形。公司近期出品的微短剧《开标之战》投资规模较小，截至目前其所产生的归属于公司的收入约50万元，预计未来在公司整体营业收入中占比较小，不会对公司经营业绩产生较大影响。公司短剧业务规模较小，2025年度盈利情况为亏损；公司海外业务规模亦较小，收入占比不足1%，敬请广大投资者注意投资风险。截至本公告披露日，公司AIGC平台尚未形成相关收入；预计在未来一段时间内，该业务对公司生产经营与财务状况不构成重大影响，敬请广大投资者注意投资风险。
其他重要内容：
国际能源署：全球柴油供应紧张将持续至2027年
10月14日，国际能源署发布月度石油市场报告说，受中东和俄罗斯柴油出口持续受阻等因素影响，全球柴油市场供应紧张局面加剧，库存持续下降，柴油供应紧张态势预计将持续至2027年。
9月份中国货物贸易进出口首破5万亿元，增长27.5%

articles.title: The Download: faking blood and the future of batteries
articles.text:
This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
The US military’s race to make fake blood
In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members. The mission was a reminder of the risks of transporting blood, which has a limited shelf life and is often in short supply.
Now, a $73 million DARPA effort aims to create shelf-stable versions of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells. The idea is to develop dried blood products that can be stored for long periods and deployed quickly on the battlefield.
The project aims to have bags of dried blood products deployed in the field by 2029. But getting it all done will be tough, and researchers still have major questions about the safety and effectiveness of synthetic alternatives.
Discover how the military hopes to make blood last longer.
—Andrew Rosenblum
This story is from the next issue of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get your hands on a copy as soon as it lands on Wednesday, October 21!
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: WeLion New Energy and its semi-solid-state batteries
WeLion New Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
WeLion New Energy is on a quest to make safer, better batteries. The Chinese company’s liquid-solid hybrid cells aim to pack more power into electric cars, boats and drones, potentially improving safety and offering greater energy density than lithium-ion batteries.
In 2023, WeLion released a battery pack with EV-maker Nio that offered a range of over 1,000 kilometers. Now, the company is developing batteries with even higher energy density. But scaling up production and competing on cost remain major challenges.
Explore WeLion’s push to make safer, higher-capacity batteries.
—You Xiaoying
Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch, spanning everything from geothermal power plants to carbon dioxide batteries.
MIT Technology Review Narrated: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers
Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also slow the aging process.
Drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their GLP-1 drugs age less quickly, according to molecular “aging clocks” that track changes in DNA or levels of key proteins.
The findings add to speculation that GLP-1 drugs could be acting on basic causes of aging and might be true longevity treatments. But how much can we read into these results?
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 The FBI has arrested an OpenAI engineer accused of snooping
A Saudi national is accused of planting a covert recording device. (Guardian)
+ The camera-and-microphone tool sells online for $13.99. (Gizmodo)
+ It was allegedly discovered plugged into a TV’s USB port. (Verge)
+ He reportedly used chatbots to plan the covert recording. (Wired $)
+ OpenAI says its AI models helped identify the employee. (Reuters $)
2 Ukrainian drones have hit Russia’s largest data centre
But Sberbank claims its systems and services were not disrupted. (Reuters $)
+ Ukraine’s data center strikes have thrown Russia into turmoil. (FT $)
+ But they haven’t stopped Russian bot farms from trolling. (Verge)
+ Europe has a drone-filled vision for future wars. (MIT Technology Review)
3 Weight-loss drugs are being tweaked to treat brain disorders
New GLP-1 trials are targeting addiction and depression. (Nature)
+ But we’re still figuring out their side effects. (MIT Technology Review)
4 Tesla robotaxis have been accused of speeding in school zones
US regulators are reviewing the claims. (Verge)
+ Tesla’s security features thwarted a federal tracking attempt. (404 Media)
5 US defense startups are turning to Taiwan to build China-free drones
At least 13 joint agreements have been signed since 2025.  (WSJ $)
+ Taiwan’s “silicon shield” could be weakening. (MIT Technology Review)
6 A war game  exposed the risks of a solar geoengineering arms race
Participants feuded over rules for dimming the sun. (Wired $)
+ Geoengineering also faces practical challenges. (MIT Technology Review)
7 AI company Character.ai has filed for bankruptcy
It’s been accused of stealing content and harming kids. (CNBC)
+ Disney has offered $20 million for its chatbot tech. (Ars Technica)
+ Its filings expose common issues with AI business models. (404 Media)
8 Apple has a new smart-home lineup built around a revamped Siri
HomeView pairs a 7-inch screen with face recognition. (Guardian
+ While the Home Collection adds cameras, locks, and thermostats. (Wired $)
+ Siri AI powers the experience, but still needs to prove its smarts. (WSJ $)
9 Scientists have identified a new dinosaur in a century-old fossil
Invictibellatrix amberina may be Europe’s first megaraptoran. (New Scientist $)
10 SpaceX’s latest launch lit up the skies with a “space jellyfish”
Rocket exhaust expanded into tentacles high in the atmosphere. (WP $)
Quote of the day
“It is like a thumb on the scale that we haven’t really ever seen.”
—Danielle Citron, a University of Virginia law professor, tells The Washington Post that Elon Musk’s ability to amplify conspiracy theories on X could give misinformation an unprecedented influence in the midterms.
One more thing
Is the Pentagon allowed to surveil Americans with AI?
The ongoing public feud between the Department of Defense and the AI company Anthropic has raised a deep and still unanswered question: Does the law actually allow the US government to conduct mass surveillance on Americans?
Surprisingly, the answer is not straightforward. More than a decade after Edward Snowden exposed the NSA’s collection of bulk metadata from the phones of Americans, the US is still navigating a gap between what ordinary people think and what the law allows.
Today, the legal complexity has a new edge: AI is supercharging surveillance—and our laws haven’t caught up. Here’s how the Pentagon’s use of AI has exposed legal gray areas.
—Michelle Kim
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)

articles.title: TeachGrade: Training-Free Short Answer Scoring with Teacher Evidence
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14900v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Multi-subject, multi-step scoring requires consistent partial credit across grading conventions. We introduce TeachGrade, a training-free framework using teacher-graded examples. The Task Adapt module builds two frozen memories: Skill captures contextual teacher preferences beyond the rubric; CaseBank supplies local evidence. PreJudge provides retrieval cues; FinalJudge regrades the answer without preliminary scores. On 3,829 SAS-Bench answers across 12 tasks, official macro collaborative consistency score (CCS) rises from Native's 67.99 to 81.32 (+13.33 points), and pooled step exact match from 54.85% to 62.71%. Macro quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) reaches 84.71, exceeding Native, OpenJudge, ProofGrader, and Trojsten by 9.52, 3.50, 11.37, and 17.43 points, respectively, and leading on 8 tasks. Local Qwen3.8-27B gains 8.83 CCS and 4.08 QWK points, improving CCS on all 12 tasks. QWK gains over Native span 6.38--14.65 points on Portuguese automatic essay scoring (AES) and 2.16--2.24 on ASAP-SAS across label views, with lower mean absolute error. These results support reuse across languages, response formats, and backbones without weight updates.

articles.title: Nvidia GPU prices spike in Japan; prices up to 41% higher than Amazon US
articles.text:
A Redditor has shared a photograph of the prices of Nvidia RTX 50-series GPUs in Japan, and it doesn’t bode well for gamers. According to u/Chaise91’s post on the r/pcmasterrace subreddit, retail prices for some of the best gaming GPUs are somewhere between 5.66% and 41.1% higher compared to Amazon U.S. listings.
The memory chip shortage and massive demand for AI compute have been affecting the supply of gaming GPUs, with reports suggesting Nvidia is planning to halt RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs. Because of this, the supply of high-end GPUs has vanished online, with third-party sellers now demanding almost $10,000 if you want to buy one. The image shared on the social media platform does not show the RTX 5090, so we fear that retailers in the market no longer have the high-end graphics card in stock, leading to supply pressure on the lower-tier cards.
We built a table comparing the prices from the Japanese retailer to listings we found on Amazon based on the current exchange rate of JPY 153.38 for every USD 1, and the hikes vary between 12.71% on average for the RTX 5080 to a jaw-dropping 41.10% for the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB. Note that these are pre-tax prices, though, so your mileage may vary depending on which state you live in. We added a representative 8.5% tax rate to see the price difference for gamers in states with high sales taxes, and the difference falls between 3.88% and 30.04%.

articles.title: Vesta: Queueing-Aware LLM Scheduling for Real-World Workloads
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14686v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Agentic applications generate multi-turn sequences of LLM requests, with each new turn extending the context accumulated from prior interactions and tool calls. Prefix caching reuses the KV cache of earlier turns and avoids redundant prefill, but routing every turn to its cache-affine instance can create severe local queues while capacity remains idle elsewhere. Remote KV cache access relaxes this tension, yet migrating execution adds transfer work and is harmful when the cluster is already congested. Thus, deciding where to execute a request requires reasoning jointly about cache locality, queueing, and the current operating point of the cluster.
We present Vesta, a queueing-aware scheduler for distributed agentic LLM serving. Vesta assigns each session a stable holder for its authoritative KV cache while independently selecting an executor for every request. Grounded in classical queueing theory, its objective accounts for backlog, reusable prefixes, KV cache transfer, and the queueing externality of additional service demand; it migrates execution to recover idle capacity when beneficial and favors placements that add the least prefill and transfer work as congestion rises. Vesta also migrates reusable prefixes across length buckets to avoid cold starts. On real-world agentic workloads, Vesta improves throughput by 14.0\% and reduces mean TTFT by 57.8\% over the state-of-the-art scheduler in a PD-colocated deployment. In PD-disaggregated deployments, it reduces mean TTFT by up to 18.1\% and P99 TTFT by up to 29.0\% at matched throughput.

导语：10月14日，腾讯旗下两大用户规模领先的办公产品——企业微信与 WorkBuddy 联合发布新版本，实现双向深度联合。
10月14日，腾讯旗下两大用户规模领先的办公产品——企业微信与 WorkBuddy 联合发布新版本，实现双向深度联合。此次升级后，WorkBuddy 正式进入企业微信通讯录，可调用企微的工作上下文，二者共用一套企业微信账号体系。此次更新将腾讯长期积累的连接能力，与智能体的理解和执行能力结合，深入企业实际场景。目前，企业微信已覆盖超过 1400 万真实企业与组织，每日通过企业微信服务的微信用户达 7.5 亿。企业无需更换平台、迁移数据或改变工作习惯，就能在熟悉的工作方式中用上AI实现效率提升。
连接全域上下文，AI进入办公现场成为真实生产力
在全新发布的企业微信 5.0.12版本中，WorkBuddy将以可对话机器人的身份进入企业联系人列表，用户可以随时通过聊天的方式处理任务；同时，最新5.8.0版本的WorkBuddy同步支持企业微信账号登录，在企业授权范围内，获得包括消息、文档、会议、网盘在内的十大能力权限，完成深度分析、复杂文档处理等多种任务。
企业经营的“全域上下文”，不只有文档和会议等内部协同数据，还包括与外部客户相连的需求、服务和业务反馈。基于企业微信连接内外的独特优势，WorkBuddy真正获得了企业全域上下文，参与项目协作、业务流程与客户服务，推动任务流转、发现客户商机，让AI从办公提效走向提升企业经营的组织生产力。
AI从个人提效迈向统一部署，企业数据更加安全可控
对于企业而言，AI 使用不再是分散的个人选择。账号体系的打通意味着在企业微信内，管理员可以统一配置企业的 WorkBuddy 机器人，进行账号分配、用量管理及 AI 算力采购。根据员工的组织身份，设置不同人员的访问权限，并限制 AI 访问高敏感信息，更清晰地界定数据流转路径与责任边界，使信息更加安全可控。
在提供一整套AI办公解决方案同时，腾讯也为企业提供了更开放的AI生态和平台能力。企业微信与 WorkBuddy 支持多模型、多 Agent 的开放选择，企业可按岗位和业务场景组合 AI 能力。此外，基于WorkBuddy企业版办公套件，企业客户还可以一键打通腾讯文档、腾讯乐享、腾讯网盘、安全与效能运营平台、腾讯 AI 设计智能体 Ardot 等协同办公套件帐号，实现办公记忆和数据共享、一个Agent底座实现体验及管理后台同步。
目前，新版本互通能力面向企业微信已认证企业开放，并提供限免体验名额，企业可领取、申请开通或统一采购。欧莱雅、麦当劳、比亚迪等企业正探索落地“企业微信 + WorkBuddy”方案。

articles.title: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14705v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models have advanced medical reasoning, but clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains challenging because prescription decisions require integrating domain knowledge, syndrome differentiation, treatment principles, herbal prescription composition, and dosage determination. We develop a TCM language model family comprising models with 4 billion, 8 billion, and 14 billion parameters. The artificial intelligence contribution is a staged clinical alignment framework integrating large scale continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, complementary reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning (RL). We further formulate herbal prescription generation as a structured RL problem with prescription-level feedback, enabling direct optimization of clinical decision outputs beyond knowledge reproduction and generic instruction following. The engineering application is TCM clinical decision support, particularly herbal prescription recommendation. We evaluate the models on a public benchmark containing 25,620 expert-verified items across 13 TCM knowledge and clinical reasoning tasks and on a private retrospective dataset of 4,348 spleen and stomach disease prescription cases. The 14 billion parameter reinforcement aligned model achieves a prescription generation F1 of 37.0 on the public benchmark, compared with 32.3 for DeepSeek-R1 with 671 billion total parameters, and a herb-level F1 of 52.8 on the clinical dataset with improved dosage agreement. Reinforcement post-training consistently improves prescription recommendation across all scales, while physician-source analysis shows that expert heterogeneity affects reward stability. These findings demonstrate a scalable pathway from domain grounding and reasoning supervision to clinically oriented prescription decision support.

articles.title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.15208v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Deep research requires connecting multiple steps of search, reasoning, and computation, with intermediate findings guiding what to investigate next. As investigations grow, agents must maintain research state across model calls and check findings before errors propagate into subsequent work. We introduce PANINI-DR, a multi-agent harness that separates coordination of the overall investigation from the research and verification of individual subquestions. A shared workspace, built on the Generative Semantic Workspace representation, records subquestions, their dependencies, findings, and supporting evidence. Researchers investigate individual subquestions, while a separate verification agent checks proposed answers against those subquestions and their evidence. Verification feedback guides further investigation, and recorded findings inform subsequent assignments. We evaluate PANINI-DR on BrowseComp-Plus, FRAMES, and MoNaCo against seven state-of-the-art deep-research harnesses, all using a shared language-model backbone and frozen corpora. PANINI-DR achieves the strongest average performance across the three benchmarks. On BrowseComp-Plus, it achieves 73.3% accuracy, outperforming the next-best harness by 16.0 points. Its advantage is strongest on hard questions, where it answers nearly twice as many as the next-best harness. Ablations further show that structured planning and persistent state improve performance, as does checking each finding against its cited evidence before it is reused. Because a model can answer correctly from memory alone, we also analyze the evidence retained by each harness. PANINI-DR achieves the highest answer recoverability from saved evidence on all three benchmarks, while complementary claim-support audits show stronger evidence-backed answers. Accounting for this evidence changes how harnesses compare and further strengthens PANINI-DR's advantage.

articles.title: 宾大茅佳源：从单次演示到 83% 真机泛化，破解具身智能数据困局｜IROS 2026
articles.text:
剖析视觉与动作脱节，引入 TR 指标与自适应引导，重构具身泛化机制。
作者丨张璐
编辑丨岑峰
在机械臂的实机测试中，不少团队都遇到过类似的困扰：为了让机器人学会抓取某个马克杯，往往需要人类抓着机械臂录入上百条示范轨迹。然而只要把杯子换成未见过的款式，或者稍微改变物体的摆放位置，策略的成功率就会急剧下降。这种靠海量遥操作数据硬堆技能的方式，很难让机器人真正具备应对新环境的泛化能力。更棘手的是，即便当前的视频预测模型已经能准确画出合理的未来画面，但一旦接入动作模块驱动实机，机械臂依然频频出错。在 IROS 2026 大会上，来自 UPenn、MIT 与 Stanford 联合团队的茅佳源分享了他们的思考。她不仅介绍了只需一次人类演示就能泛化执行多种非抓取任务的 RAPID 闭环框架，还首次提出了诊断“视觉会了、手却做不对”这一机制脱节的 TR 指标。借由基于 TR 的自适应引导机制，团队最终将双臂机器人在复杂组合任务上的真机泛化成功率提升到了 83%。以下是茅佳源的演讲分享，AI科技评论在不改变原意的情况下，进行了编辑和整理：
01
百条轨迹换一项技能，
纯数据拟合为何难做物理泛化？
过去几年，构建通用物理智能的主流思路是“数据拟合”，试图通过端到端学习，实现从视觉观察到控制动作的直接映射。这一路径虽推动了大量研究，但在面对真实复杂的物理交互时，瓶颈迅速显现。以 Actor Labs 的挖掘机实验为例，其团队将 Physical Intelligence 的 π0.5部署至挖掘机，结合工业操作员的大规模真实数据训练策略。尽管展示中仅用200 条轨迹成功完成了一项任务，但这恰恰暴露出纯数据驱动路线的缺点：数据效率极低，且多任务能力受限。如果掌握每一项单一技能都需要百小时级或数百条轨迹的数据积累，这种依靠堆叠数据推动的范式，其规模化扩展的可行性显然存疑。相比之下，人类仅凭单次演示就能理解动作背后的物理逻辑，并轻松迁移至不同尺寸、材质的物体甚至全新任务中。当端到端模型在分布外（OOD）场景中频频失灵，研究者们不得不重新审视：在盲目堆砌数据量之外，是否存在更根本的智能构建路径？这便引出了第二条路线：将智能视为世界建模与规划（Intelligence as World Modeling and Planning）。其核心在于将机器学习与物理规划相结合，使智能体通过小样本理解物理规律，进而实现真正的分布外泛化。
02
告别像素级预测，
用“神经+符号”构建可推理的世界模型
要实现基于规划的智能，首先需构建“世界模型”，即让智能体在内部建立物理世界表征，并基于该表征演推后续动作。然而，物理环境极其复杂，若直接在像素级预测未来状态与细节，计算代价会非常高，难以支持长序列动作的实时规划。破解这一难题的关键在于引入组合式抽象表示。智能体无需记忆所有像素细节，而是提炼形状、姿态、材质等抽象属性，并用状态转移图显式建立“动作-状态”演变机制。图：神经符号概念将物体抽象为形状、姿态、材质等属性，并用状态转移图描述动作导致的 state 演变。图中 s0→s1 表示 push(glass)，s1→s3 表示 flip(cap)。这就是神经符号概念的核心：
“神经”层：利用神经网络进行视觉感知，提取物体的几何与物理属性；
“符号”层：利用符号逻辑对这些属性进行组合，并定义动作与状态之间的转移规则。两者结合，智能体摆脱端到端黑盒映射，转而学习物理世界运行规律的结构化模型。有了这种抽象表示，机器人即可在执行前内部推演（如推动杯子或翻转瓶盖后的状态演变），自主规划动作序列。这正是“从单次演示中学习并强泛化”的基础。
03
破解策略网络不可拼接困局：
将动作生成转化为“约束求解”
具备可组合的世界模型后，下一个问题是：如何将高层逻辑规划转化为物理世界中可执行的具体动作？传统强化学习与端到端范式中，策略网络（π）普遍无法直接拼接。例如分别训练抓取（π1）、移动（π2）、放置（π3）三个网络，因观测空间、动作空间及中间状态难以对齐，极难直接串联完成长序列任务。针对策略不可组合的困境，替代方案并非训练更大的端到端网络，而是将动作生成重新定义为约束优化问题。在此框架下，智能体需在给定初始状态 s0 下，求解使动作代价（如轨迹长度）最小化的轨迹，同时满足两类关键约束：
路径约束：包含动力学约束 dynamics（轨迹必须符合物理定律）与无碰撞约束 collision-free（机器人与环境无干涉）；图：约束优化生成动作。路径约束包括关节限制与无碰撞；子目标约束包括抓取目标与放置目标。
子目标约束：包含阶段性接触目标 holding-target（如稳妥抓取物体）与最终任务目标 target-on-rack（如将物体精准放置至指定架子）。图 ：约束优化组合动作。目标是最小化轨迹长度 |t1|+|t2|，同时满足 dynamics、collision-free、holding-target、target-on-rack 等约束。这种设计将学习显式解耦为约束集与约束值两个层面。机器人无需从零学习物理法则（交由已知物理模型与优化求解器处理），神经网络只需聚焦与任务相关的关键约束。这种解耦大幅减轻数据负担，使模型能以极低数据量捕捉关键约束，实现跨物体与跨场景的精准求解。以团队 MAGIC 项目中的“物品悬挂”任务为例，这类操作需要同时兼顾抓取、悬挂姿态与运动轨迹三重联合约束。面对这一挑战，传统模型规划因搜索空间过大，单次求解动辄超过 5 分钟；而基于无监督特征学习与策略学习的代表性方法，哪怕在 10 万个合成水杯数据上训练，单次演示泛化成功率也仅有 42%。”相比之下，该框架通过视觉对应关系引导约束优化，仅凭单次演示就将成功率大幅提升到了 93%。图：悬挂任务中，传统模型规划单次求解超 5 分钟；纯数据驱动方法在 10 万合成 mug 上单例成功率 42%。本方法通过视觉对应将成功率提升至 93%。
04
RAPID 架构：
1 次人类演示+代码智能体，
搞定复杂非抓取交互
如果将上述“约束+接触序列”的思路进一步推演，就能构建出面向更复杂物理交互的通用架构：RAPID。注：RAPID源于此篇论文。点击查看：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.30249图：RAPID 面向接触丰富、非抓取操作，仅需单次人类演示即可学习。在 RAPID 架构中，技能学习被转化为由编程智能体与物理校验器构成的闭环编程循环：1.演示解析与原语拆解：从单次演示中提取动作，自动切分为推、翻转、支点旋转、抓取等基础操作原语；2.以物体为中心的程序生成：Coding Agent 将原语转化为以物体为中心的约束程序，脱离特定的几何参数，使其天然具备可复用性与组合性；3.仿真校验与闭环迭代：校验器在 Real2Sim 仿真环境中验证程序，将碰撞、物理可行性等反馈传给 Coding Agent 进行修正，可在部署前筛除大量物理不可行程序。图：RAPID 的智能体编程循环。Coding Agent 生成行为程序 Π，Evaluator 在 Real2Sim 仿真中校验并反馈，迭代修正。在涵盖书架、隔板等场景的 8 个复杂非抓取真机任务中（灵活组合了推、翻、压移、支点、倾倒、抓取等原语），RAPID 仅凭单次人类演示，便展现出极高的鲁棒性与泛化求解能力。这说明，将 Coding Agent 的代码生成能力与物理模型校验相结合，能以符号化约束优化实现强泛化的单示例学习。  雷峰网
05
大模型盲区：
为何视频-动作模型无法自动“涌现”组合力？
RAPID 框架展示了 Coding Agent 在复杂物理操作任务中的能力：通过结合物理验证器、约束求解等模块，系统能够仅凭单次人类演示规划并执行复杂的非抓取操作。RAPID 本身也是一个模块化系统，其能力来自 Coding Agent 与不同功能模块之间的协作。这说明，组合性不仅体现在运动技能的组合上，也体现在系统如何组织和调用不同的能力模块。由此引出了一个更一般的问题：面向实际任务，我们应该如何设计这样的模块化系统？哪些能力应该被拆分为独立模块，模块之间又应该通过什么接口协作？与完全端到端的神经网络相比，模块化系统能够引入显式结构，使各个环节更易于解释、验证和替换，但也可能受到人工划分和接口设计的限制；端到端模型则能够联合学习感知到动作的映射，却更难对中间过程进行独立检查与干预。理解这两种范式在泛化能力、数据效率和系统鲁棒性上的优势与局限，是将智能体应用于真实物理世界的重要问题。在探索组合性的另一条路上，模块化系统展现出了独特优势。例如，系统可以先用开放词汇检测器提取“马克杯”的视觉掩码，再交由特定策略完成抓取，这就是模块化组合的直观体现。以团队此前发表的 Retriever 框架为例，它将感知、推理与控制拆分为独立模块，并显式建模触发器与缓冲区，巧妙解决了多频率异步（如腕部相机 30Hz、机器人状态 60Hz、低阶技能 2Hz）下的闭环控制难题，在双臂机器人“给牛排撒调料”等长时程任务中验证了模块组合的高效性。   但是，各模块之间受限的信息流动，使其难以充分吸收不同任务之间的协同效应。   这就引发了一个更深度的思考：神经网络能否直接将感知、记忆、规划与控制融为一体？如果放弃人工预定义的原语与模块划分，转向端到端统一的多模态大模型，将包含丰富物理规律的视频预测与动作生成联合训练，组合能力能否在模型中自动“涌现”？围绕这一课题，团队展开了两次尝试。第一次是视频生成预测+动作控制器；第二次是视频-动作联合训练模型。然而，随后的实机与仿真实验表明，问题的复杂程度远超预想。
▎试错一：视觉预测转动作指令，难以胜任富接触操作为了吸收跨任务的协同效应，研究团队展开了第一次尝试：利用通用的视频生成模型预测未来画面，再将视觉预测翻译为机器人的具体动作。   这一路线对应团队发表于 ICLR 2024 (Spotlight) 的 AVDC 框架。原文链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.08576其动作提取流程分为三个核心阶段：  1.视频预测：输入语言指令与当前 RGB-D 观察，利用预训练视频预测模型生成未来数帧的视频；   2.稠密运动估计：从合成的未来视频帧中计算光流，结合深度信息进行 SE(3) 空间位姿估计，恢复出物体的三维运动轨迹；   3.笛卡尔控制映射：根据物体的 3D 轨迹反推机器人末端执行器的移动方向，生成笛卡尔空间下的控制指令。 该架构最大的优势在于摆脱了对显式动作标签的依赖。模型可以直接利用无动作标签的视频数据进行预训练，并迁移至机器人任务中。同时，由于它提取的是物体本身的三维运动而非特定机械臂的关节点位，因而具备出色的跨本体泛化能力。然而，真机测试揭示了这一解耦范式的明显局限：它主要支持基础的抓取、移动与放置技能。   面对翻转、按压、支点旋转等复杂的富接触操作，单纯依靠像素层面的视频预测，难以捕捉真实的物理受力与精准的接触作用点。   这表明，“视频生成→动作翻译”这种串联管线无法自动涌现出复杂的组合行为。必须打破解耦，将视频预测与动作生成深度结合进行联合训练——这便引出了第二次尝试：视频-动作联合模型。
▎试错二：看懂了未来画面，Action Head却还在“盲开”为了克服单一视频驱动无法处理复杂接触动作的痛点，研究团队展开了第二次尝试：构建视频-动作联合模型。   这一架构的初衷，是让负责动作生成的网络能够直接“看到”并利用视频模型对未来的物理预测。   在具体设计上，团队采用预训练视频预测模型 Cosmos Predict 2.5-2B（基于 Flow Matching 架构）作为骨干网络。在视频生成的去噪过程中，提取中间噪声水平σ_v下的潜特征，经由特征投影层后，与机器人的本体状态以及含噪动作 Token 一同送入 Gemma Action Head，最终通过 Flow Matching 联合生成去噪后的动作控制 Token。   然而，实机与仿真实验给出了出乎意料的结论：统一的视频-动作联合模型，并不会自动“涌现”出组合泛化能力。   团队观察到了两个棘手的问题：1.视觉能泛化，执行却失效：视频预测模型本身具备优秀的泛化能力，面对未见过的指令时，能生成合理的视觉未来帧。然而，一旦接入 Action Head 驱动机械臂实际执行，策略在组合式分布外任务上的成功率便急剧下跌。   2.极高的超参数敏感度与 ID-OOD 权衡：训练配方对性能有决定性影响。例如，LoRA 联合训练能在 ID（分布内）与组合 OOD 之间达成某种权衡，而全参数微调则更容易偏向 ID 性能，牺牲泛化。  深入分析“泛化鸿沟”后，团队发现，Action Head 在生成控制动作时，常常倾向于直接“忽略”视频模型预测出的未来特征。   在对比实验中，哪怕视频模型预测出了完全错误的未来画面，Action Head 依然可能偶然完成动作；反之，当视频模型生成了完美正确的未来画面时，Action Head 却反而给出了错误的动作控制。   这证实了动作生成与未来预测之间存在严重的“机制脱节”，视频预测中蕴含的物理知识，未能有效地转化为控制端的泛化能力。
▎诊断：引入时间比率，看穿动作头有没有“偷懒”为了精准量化 Action Head 在决策时到底有多依赖视频模型的未来预测，研究团队提出了一个直观且量化的诊断指标：时间比率（Temporal Ratio，TR）TR = 未来帧的注意力权重 / 当前帧的注意力权重  注：此篇论文提出的TR这一诊断指标，点击查看原文：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.08127该指标直接反映了动作头的决策偏好。TR 越高，说明 Action Head 越认真地“看”视频模型预测出的未来画面并据此导向动作；TR 越低，则说明动作头几乎在“盲开”，完全忽视未来的预测信息。   通过分析不同模型与超参数配置下的 TR 曲线，团队发现了一个关键规律：峰值 TR（Peak TR）精准预测了模型的组合泛化能力。TR 越高的模型，其在分布外任务上的成功率就越强；而那些 TR 极低的模型，泛化成功率几乎为零。研究人员通过调整视频噪声水平σ_v来人工抬升 TR，同一个模型的 OOD 成功率也随之呈现出明确的攀升趋势。此外，TR 并非静态常数，而是在任务执行过程中动态演变。通常在执行前几步 TR 会升至峰值，模型积极参考未来规划；随后随 Replanning Step 推进而回落。
▎免重训修复方案：TR 自适应强引导，真机 OOD 成功率提升至 83%找到了“机制脱节”的病灶后，研究团队提出了一种无需重新训练模型即可弥合泛化鸿沟的方案：自适应引导。   团队将无分类器引导（CFG）拓展为两个维度的强引导：语言引导与计划引导。与固定权重的传统引导不同，自适应引导会实时监测 TR 指标：当检测到 TR 出现峰值、动作头正积极参考未来规划时，系统会自动调大计划与语言引导的权重，强化未来物理约束；而在 TR 处于低位的平稳阶段则不叠加额外引导。这种“在关键决策点精准发力”的机制，既避免了过度引导对分布内（ID）性能的损伤，又大幅提升了模型在空间、物体和目标分布外（OOD）任务上的组合泛化能力。在 LIBERO 仿真基准上的测试证明了该机制的优越性。传统的“平坦引导”（Flat Guidance，即固定权重的引导）虽然能提升分布外（OOD）的成功率，但会严重损害分布内（ID）的性能；而自适应引导通过 TR 的动态调节，在保持分布内较高成功率的同时，大幅提升了在空间、物体和目标分布外任务上的组合泛化表现，实现了更好的 ID 与 OOD 性能权衡。  随后，团队在搭载双臂机器人的真实物理环境（基于 YAM 硬件与 abc.bot 数据集）中评估了 8 项复杂任务，涵盖从纸袋中取出瓶子、整理零食到货架、折叠 T 恤等。在未见过的组合式分布外任务（如“把水果放进纸袋”）中，对比模型 Cosmos-Policy 的平均成功率仅约 12%，而团队自己的模型在未引导前平均成功率为 71.8%，引入基于 TR 的自适应引导后，真机泛化成功率进一步提升至 83%，验证了该方案在真实物理场景中的有效性。
06
结语：走向通用物理智能，
核心不在于盲目堆叠数据
视频预测与动作控制之间的协同效应，并不会在联合训练中自动“涌现”出来。我们看到，不同的模型架构与训练配方会带来不同水平的组合泛化能力，且往往伴随着分布内（ID）与分布外（OOD）性能之间的权衡。虽然我们提出的时间比率（TR）提供了一个精准的诊断工具，但要真正弥合泛化鸿沟，我们必须重新审视“组合性”本身：从架构、优化目标到数据定义的根本层面进行重构。   回到最本质的范式选择上，模块化系统依然非常强大。它天生具备显式的结构化组合性、较高的数据效率，以及对实时机器人系统至关重要的异步控制能力。但它的局限在于，无法充分吸收不同任务之间的深层协同效应。   因此，如何将模块化系统“强组合性与高数据效率”的优势，与统一大模型“全局吸收协同”的潜力有机结合，是我们接下来最核心的研究方向。   这背后依然有一系列深层的科学问题等待我们去解答：
前馈神经网络究竟能否涌现出组合性？
这种涌现出的组合性，能否实现高数据效率的学习？
我们该如何形式化真实物理世界中的复杂噪声与多模态数据？
我们又该如何形式化泛化标准？究竟是以最坏情况还是平均情况来评估？   把这些底层逻辑厘清，我们才能真正走向通用物理智能。

articles.title: Modder injects leaked DLSS 5 4x Multipass on 1996 Quake
articles.text:
A Ukrainian DLSS 5 experimenter is back at it again, this time testing the original Quake game. It’s running as a post-process, not natively integrated into the game engine, using 4x Multipass to enhance the effect, but it doesn’t look so good.
Valery Kryzhanovsky has posted multiple videos running DLSS 5 on games it was never meant to be used for, nor were the games built with AI upscaling and image enhancements in mind. We previously covered a few of Valery’s projects, running DLSS 5 on 2D games like Duke Nukem and Pac-Man, resulting in weird and cursed images.
However, this time Valery uploaded a video of it on the 1996 Quake, considered to be the very first true 3D FPS in history. Valery explains in the description that the game is not running the leaked DLSS 5 build natively, but as a post-process using ReShade through RenoDX to play with the parameters and settings and inject the effect on DOSBox’s rendered frame. So it’s an emulated version of Quake with basically an AI filter with the DLSS 5 algorithm over it four times, except it’s running in real time on a game. This is similar to how others have experimented with DLSS 5 on videos, applying the effect on top, like JackSpace’s video to “fix” bad CGI in old movies with DLSS 5.
Before DLSS’ popularity, Nvidia released an RTX demo running Quake II with ray tracing in the game engine to improve the lighting. That demo looked stunning, with realistic lighting and reflections, but DLSS is not ray tracing/RTX; it’s an upscaling technology that runs well on RTX cores. And on top of that, DLSS 5 is not even integrated into Quake’s engine, explaining the terrible results. However, this is a very early build of DLSS 5, and Valery says in his blog that the leaked build is undertrained. I honestly thought it would do better, considering there are more obvious 3D elements for the upscaler to work with compared to the 2D games Valery has experimented with. It seems that it darkens everything so much, possibly because of the sparse distribution of torches and highlights.
This might fare better if DLSS 5 were integrated into the engine, like how Sultim Tsyrendashiev modded ray tracing into Quake's engine, similar to Nvidia's Quake II demo.
Earlier this week, Nvidia announced that it had improved the performance of its DLSS 5 model by 2x, while shrinking its footprint by 24%. The result should be higher FPS while using less VRAM, drastically increasing performance.

articles.title: Elon Musk's Terafab will reportedly receive its first EUV tool from ASML in mid-2027
articles.text:
Elon Musk's Terafab will get its first EUV lithography tool in the middle of next year, reports Tim Culpan, citing sources with knowledge of the matter. But considering that the shell of the firm's development fab will not be completed until late 2027 and that tools will only begin to be moved in later that year, according to SemiAnalysis, the scanner will sit idle for some time.
Tesla broke ground on its research fab on the north campus of Giga Texas near Austin this past April. SemiAnalysis expects the building to be completed in 15 months and predicts it will take Tesla a further six months to install equipment and production tools, after which it will be able to start processing wafers, or rather experimenting with chip production to get the team prepared for completion of the Terafab volume fab phase 1.
Given how hard it is to get an ASML Twinscan NXE EUV lithography tool these days, storing it for several months before putting it to use may sound like an expensive slack period, but it's not the significant financial problem for Terafab that it would be for a traditional chipmaker.
The projected delivery of a conventional EUV lithography system to Terafab also indicates that while Elon Musk has praised free electron laser (FEL) light sources for lithography tools, the first-generation efforts of his semiconductor production company will rely on more traditional equipment. This is not particularly surprising, as Terafab is set to use Intel's 14A manufacturing technology. 14A will use not only existing Low-NA EUV scanners, but also next-generation High-NA EUV machines.
Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking
(Image credit: tsmc)
Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecks
Leading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and Samsung
ASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examined
Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined
Using lithography systems with unconventional and largely untested light sources would require substantial modifications to the manufacturing process, extensive equipment qualification, and potentially changes to photomasks and photoresists, which would complicate the transfer of Intel’s 14A technology and delay Terafab's production ramp.
But usage of standard lithography equipment does not mean that Musk's company has no plans to use tools that are different from those used by Intel, though for now it is too early to make guesses about what Terafab engineers might change in terms of fab configuration.
SpaceX announced that it had selected Grimes County for Terafab in early August 2026. By now, there is evidence that work has progressed beyond clearing land, as drone footage published by Joe Tegtmeyer in mid-September showed foundation excavation and rebar cage installation at the northwestern part of the site. This suggests that contractors had begun structural construction by early September, although the precise purpose of the foundation is unknown.
Right now, SemiAnalysis reports that project Terafab Grimes phase 1 will be built in 20 months, equipped in 17 months, and ramped to volume in six months. Analysts project that the fab will begin operation in late 2029 and then ramped to volume by mid-2030.
An interesting note about Terafab's volume fab is that SpaceX reportedly ordered semiconductor manufacturing equipment in April 2026, several months before officially announcing the Grimes County location. This indicates that the company committed to its manufacturing plans well before the public groundbreaking. In addition, this makes the mid-2028 equipment installation forecast plausible, given the long lead times associated with advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Intel plans to begin risk production using its 14A (1.4nm-class) fabrication process in the second half of 2027 and initiate high-volume manufacturing (HVM) in the second half of 2028 if everything goes as planned. This puts Intel's ramp into HVM at least 1.5 years ahead of SpaceX’s Terafab Grimes Phase 1.
This means that while Terafab will get a proven advanced manufacturing technology, presumably with decent yields, it will not be the absolute best production node at the time, as TSMC intends to start volume production of chips using its A12 fabrication process in late 2029. A12 is a 1.2nm-class process with TSMC's second-generation nanosheet GAA transistors and backside power delivery. Intel will be close to unveiling its 14A-P node at the same time.
Nonetheless, since Terafab will likely exclusively serve SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI, a slightly less advanced node will not be a big problem for the company, as the potential cost increases incurred by using a more sophisticated manufacturing technology will be offset by using an in-house production facility.

articles.title: Linux 之父托瓦兹推出首个 AI 辅助开发的补丁：并发文件读取吞吐量提升约 3 倍
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，科技媒体 lwn 昨日（10 月 14 日）发布博文，报道称 Linux 之父林纳斯 · 托瓦兹（Linus Torvalds）在其个人 Git 仓库中推送了一个名为 noref-filemap-read-with-llm 的新开发分支，正式提交了他首个由大语言模型（LLM）辅助开发的内核补丁系列。
该媒体指出在通常情况下，在 torvalds / linux.git 仓库中，托瓦兹只维护 master 分支，很少在分支上开发，不过在最新出现 noref-filemap-read-with-llm 分支，且后缀包含“llm”，这是他在人工智能 / LLM（特别是 Claude Code）的帮助下进行的一些内核改进。
托瓦兹于 10 月 13 日在该分支下提交新的补丁，主题为“提高页面引用计数可扩展性”，主要解决 Linux 内存管理长期瓶颈。在多个线程同时高频微量读取同一个文件时候，传统机制因反复触发表级缓存（Page Cache）的引用计数更新，极易导致多核 CPU 产生严重竞态争抢。
托瓦兹坦言，这组补丁的核心代码、测试程序、漏洞审查以及公告文档的初稿，全部是在他本人的亲自指导下，由 Anthropic 推出的 AI 编程工具 Claude Code 协作完成的。
托瓦兹在关闭其电脑的部分安全防护后测试，在 8 个线程同时读取同一个文件的特定测试负载下，读取吞吐量从原本的每秒 990 万 ~1040 万次，直接跃升到了 3000 万 ~3300 万次（相当于从约 10M 飙升至 30M+），性能提升约 3 倍；同时，单次读取消耗的内核时钟周期也从大约 2950 次锐减至 725 次。
IT之家注：该补丁目前仍处于实验性分支，尚未合入 Linux 7.4 的正式主线。
不仅如此，在近期维护者峰会（Maintainers Summit）及另一处 assoc_array 代码库清理中，托瓦兹同样利用 LLM 将晦涩难懂的陈旧代码重构，甚至一口气揪出了藏匿在 Linux 系统中长达 13 年之久（可追溯至 2013 年首个提交）的 3 个隐蔽 Bug。

articles.title: Dynamo v1.5.0-motif-3-dev.2

Release Notes
Dynamo v1.5.0-motif-3-dev.2 is an experimental snapshot build with early Motif-3 NVFP4 support on the Dynamo vLLM backend. It is not recommended for production and is not a QA-gated release. APIs, behavior, and defaults may change before stable support. Use it for evaluation, testing, and early feedback only.
Summary
Dynamo v1.5.0-motif-3-dev.2 serves Motif-Technologies/Motif-3-NVFP4 on Dynamo vLLM. The amd64 CUDA 13.0 runtime is built on Motif's vLLM v0.26.0-motif3 base, with vLLM-Omni disabled, and installs NIXL v1.3.2. The image bakes in Motif NIXL compatibility fixes: KV-cache rank follows the attention backend's MLA flag (rank 3 for MLA, rank 4 otherwise), and Motif keeps its NHD cache layout (#16291).
Kubernetes recipes cover aggregated serving on two B200 GPUs and disaggregated 3P1D serving on eight B200 GPUs: three TP2 prefill workers and one TP2 decode worker, with KV-aware routing and NIXL transfer. Both profiles use expert parallelism, MTP2, an FP8 KV cache, a 262,144-token context, prefix caching, and a shared model cache. The 3P1D recipe from #16314 is on this branch in #16392 (recipe folder).

About Motif-3
Motif-3 NVFP4 is Motif Technologies' preview checkpoint published on Hugging Face as Motif-Technologies/Motif-3-NVFP4. This build serves it through Dynamo's vLLM backend as either an aggregated two-GPU B200 deployment or an eight-GPU 3P1D deployment with KV-aware routing.

vLLM Backend
Motif NIXL compatibility: The runtime image patches the pinned Motif vLLM source during the build so workers can transfer KV cache without a writable source tree. Cache-rank checks use the attention backend's MLA flag, and Motif retains the NHD layout (#16291).
Recipes
Motif-3 NVFP4 recipes: recipes/motif-3 includes a shared model-cache PVC and Hugging Face download Job, an aggregated B200 chat profile, and a disaggregated 3P1D profile with KV-aware routing and NIXL transfer. Both default to real MTP2 verification. An optional synthetic acceptance length of 2.13 is available for benchmarking, including a concurrency-64 disaggregated run with a 32-request warmup (recipe folder, README, #16392, #16314).
Getting Started
Deployment is Kubernetes-based (Dynamo Platform + DynamoGraphDeployment). Full steps — namespace, hf-token-secret, model-cache PVC, download Job, aggregated or 3P1D apply, and a /v1/chat/completions smoke test — are in the recipe README and the Fern guide. The download Job is the only step that needs the Hugging Face token. For 3P1D, each TP2 worker occupies two GPUs on one node, and the fabric must allow NIXL/UCX transfer between nodes. Optional Nscale scheduling is a Kustomize component on the generic manifest.
Known Issues / Limitations
Experimental snapshot build — not QA-gated; not for production.
The vLLM runtime image is amd64 only, and recipes reference it by tag rather than digest.
The runtime image carries Motif-specific vLLM compatibility code. Do not replace its vLLM package with an unrelated wheel.
Disaggregated serving is validated for TP2 on both prefill and decode. Other tensor-parallel sizes are unvalidated.
Shipped manifests use real MTP verification. Results measured with synthetic acceptance length 2.13 are a benchmark-only proxy and are not reproduced by the manifests as shipped.
In the reference aggregated chat trace, 35 requests exceed the 262,144-token context limit.

articles.title: Accelerating MoE Training through Expert Placement and Replica Coordination
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14798v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Distributed training of sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) models is often bottlenecked by workload imbalance and all-to-all (A2A) communication induced by dynamic token routing. Existing token deduplication, expert placement, and replication techniques alleviate these bottlenecks but do not jointly capture their distinct load semantics. Under hierarchical token deduplication, communication counts each token once per destination group at each hierarchy level, whereas expert computation processes every token-expert assignment. With replication, both costs depend jointly on physical layout and token-to-copy mapping, making separate optimization suboptimal. We present PlaceMoE to address this coupling. First, we formulate the joint optimization of expert layout and source-aware token-to-copy mapping for E experts distributed across P devices, accounting for both hierarchical communication traffic and expert-compute load. Second, we develop a solver that combines co-selection-aware expert grouping, bounded dynamic programming for replica allocation, and alternating refinement of layout and mapping. Third, PlaceMoE overlaps replica-gradient synchronization with attention backward. We evaluate PlaceMoE on a 32-GPU cluster and a 64-NPU cluster using Qwen3-VL and DeepSeek-V3. Experimental results show that PlaceMoE achieves up to a 6.94x speedup in A2A communication and 1.74-2.33x speedups in end-to-end training over the state-of-the-art training framework VeOmni.

articles.title: 微软与NVIDIA联手打造：第三种PC来临 解决Token焦虑
articles.text:
快科技10月14日消息，PC产品类型已经很久没有什么新花样了，微软前两年联合Intel、AMD、高通等公司推出了AI PC的概念，结果也不了了之了，但是现在他们又搞了新东西出来了。
这就是上周的发布会上，微软联合NVIDIA发布的RTX Spark产品，微软自己有Surface版Spark PC，其他PC厂商也会推出自己的Spark电脑，包括笔记本及主机等类型。
这种PC产品有什么不同？PCMag网站今天发了一篇雄文夸了RTX Spark PC的意义，微软把这种类型的PC称之为Builder PC（构建者PC）。
PCMag认为当前的AI硬件有三个层次，之前的PC产品大家都熟悉了，首先是Consumer AI PC消费级AI PC，这个就是微软之前吹了两年的Coplit+PC了，特征是有40-50TOPS性能的NPU单元，16-32GB内存，不过各厂商已经不怎么提这个概念了。
第二个层级是工作站/游戏本，主要特征是引入了专用GPU，用并行能力来处理AI负载，但受限于显存容量，通常就12到24GB，极个别有32GB容量，限制了上下文。
第三个层级就是Build PC代表的Big-Memory Local AI Systems大内存本地AI系统，代表性产品就是工作站开发机、苹果M系列Mac及现在的RTX Spark PC.
特点是支持大容量高带宽统一内存池，最大可达128GB，超越了传统的显存瓶颈，支持数十亿参数的大模型及庞大的上下文窗口在本地运行，无需发送数据到云计算中心。
为了提升Builder PC的体验，微软及NVIDIA分别在软件及硬件上做了大量优化，Win11专门支持MXC沙箱技术，提升了安全性，还给OpenClaw这样的Agent简化了配置过程，方便管理。
NVIDIA那边也做了深度适配，甚至承诺在使用电池的情况下也能发挥99%的RTX Spark性能，它本身还有128GB最大内存及1PFLOPS的AI性能，跑AI性能与效能兼具。
不过PCMag这篇文章更像是给未来几天要发的评测文章做铺垫，现在没有明确的价格及性能等信息，也不好判断RTX Spark的表现。
对于这种能跑大型AI的本地AI主机来说，市场需求肯定是有的，然而现在的一大问题是问世的时机太糟糕了，内存、闪存大涨价不说，先进芯片价格也涨了，RTX Spark的价格很难有什么吸引力，而且跟Mac Pro的竞争也面临着生态上的劣势。
以RTX Spark的价格来算，普通人除非AI用量极其大，否则买这种Builder PC肯定是不划算的，只有Token用量大的人可以实现Token自由，缓解Token不足带来的焦虑症。

articles.title: 32GB of DDR5 6000 RAM now costs $450
articles.text:
The AI-induced PC component shortage, which has caused drastic increases in the cost of DIY building, continues to get worse. Since last year, RAM prices have increased by more than 500% and show no sign of slowing down. In August, we reported that DDR5 6000 RAM — the sweet spot benchmark for both performance and pricing — had reached $400; now, the price is $450.
Save by going slower: CORSAIR Vengeance RGB 32GB (2 x 16GB) DDR5 5200 - $399 at Newegg
As mentioned, because DDR5 6000 RAM is a de facto standard configuration and capacity in terms of performance, tracking the price of this particular spec has proven to be a strong barometer of the industry overall. While we track RAM prices across multiple models and kits, we also track the price of 32GB DDR5 6000 RAM daily.
We've been creeping closer to $450 for some time. As of today, the cheapest 32GB DDR5 6000 kit on the market costs $449.97, or three cents shy of $450. Cheaper RAM is still available; this 32GB DDR5 4800 kit is $399 at Corsair, but good, speedy RAM is now harder to buy than ever before. The 4800 Corsair kit once cost just $80.
As RAM prices and other component hikes have a knock-on effect on PC pricing as a whole, it was recently reported that PC shipments in 3Q26 have tumbled by a massive 20%, with the top three vendors shipping 11.6 million fewer units than the same period last year.
Combo deals remain a rare bright spot. Various Newegg bundles could save you as much as $358 when you buy RAM alongside a motherboard, CPU, and even an SSD, and we've seen a recent resurgence in stock on these.
Pre-builts also continue to offer some solace to wannabe DIY builders, with price hikes trickling down to systems more slowly. With industry figures warning that memory shortages could persist well into next year, or even last up to a decade, in the space of just 12 months RAM has gone from being a PC gaming commodity to a luxury few

Release Notes
Dynamo v1.6.0-glm-5.3-flash-dev.1 is an experimental snapshot build with early GLM-5.3-Flash support on the Dynamo SGLang backend. It is not recommended for production and is not a QA-gated release. APIs, behavior, and defaults may change before stable support. Use it for evaluation, testing, and early feedback only.
Summary
Dynamo v1.6.0-glm-5.3-flash-dev.1 serves RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on Dynamo SGLang. The container is built from lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130-runtime (CUDA 13) and applies GLM-5.3-Flash backports for prefill/decode accounting, linear-attention cache handling, SM100 PTX KDA, and Mamba slot cleanup, plus a scoped cuDNN workaround in the vision encoder. Transformers 5.19.0 and tokenizers 0.23.2 are pinned so image and video requests load Glm5NextProcessor instead of falling back to text-only tokenization (#15751).
Kubernetes recipes cover a 4-GPU aggregated profile on B200 or GB200 and a 12-GPU GB200 disaggregated profile (two TP4/EP4 prefill workers and one TP4 decode worker). Aggregated serving uses round-robin routing and accepts text, images, and video. Disaggregated serving uses KV-aware routing with worker KV events and Mooncake transfer over NVLink, and accepts text and images. All three profiles use NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, EAGLE speculative decoding with ReplaySSM, and HiCache. A shared model-cache download pins revision f46cf340d35a22d0d83d0c1dac8957cf2b1bcd35, and an AIPerf text-trace reference ships with the recipes (#15752, #16387).

About GLM-5.3-Flash
GLM-5.3-Flash is a Z.AI mixture-of-experts model (320B total parameters, 18B active) with hybrid sparse and linear attention and Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections. This preview serves the NVFP4 checkpoint RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 through Dynamo's SGLang backend, aggregated on B200 or GB200 or disaggregated on GB200.

GLM-5.3-Flash runtime: Builds the CUDA SGLang image on lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130-runtime and applies upstream backports for prefill/decode latency and retraction accounting, linear-attention hooks and cache accounting, PTX KDA safety and SM100 support, and Mamba slot cleanup before decode preallocation. A local patch disables cuDNN only around the GLM vision downsample convolution. Transformers 5.19.0 and tokenizers 0.23.2 are pinned so AutoProcessor registers Glm5NextProcessor for image and video inputs (#15751).
Recipes
GLM-5.3-Flash SGLang recipes: Added recipes/glm-5.3-flash/sglang — shared model-cache PVC and pinned Hugging Face download, B200 aggregated (agg-b200-agentic, 1x TP4), GB200 aggregated (agg-gb200-agentic, 1x TP4), and GB200 disaggregated (disagg-gb200-agentic, 2 prefill TP4/EP4 + 1 decode TP4, Mooncake over NVLink) profiles, real EAGLE verification by default, and an AIPerf text-trace reference (recipe folder, README, #15752, #16387).
Getting Started
Deployment is Kubernetes-based (Dynamo Platform and DynamoGraphDeployment). GB200 profiles also create a ComputeDomain and require the NVIDIA DRA driver. Full steps — namespace, hf-token-secret, model-cache PVC, pinned Hugging Face download, Kustomize render, DGD apply, and a /v1/chat/completions smoke test — are in the recipe README. The SGLang checkpoint is RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 and is not the checkpoint used by the sibling vLLM recipes. Recipes expect registry credentials for nvcr.io.
Known Issues / Limitations
Experimental snapshot build — not QA-gated; not for production.
The disaggregated GB200 recipe accepts text and images only. Video input is available on the aggregated B200 and GB200 recipes.
Disaggregated GB200 workers must share one NVLink clique and require the ComputeDomain CRD and NVIDIA DRA driver.
Synthetic acceptance replaces real speculative verification and is for performance experiments only.
End-to-end multimodal generation with this rebuilt image has not been validated. The image build checks that the GLM image and video processors load.
Measured performance results are not included. The recipe ships an AIPerf text-trace job only.

articles.title: Is the Future Predictable? Modeling Future Predictability for Reliable Temporal Reasoning
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14073v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain unreliable when reasoning about the future. Existing models often overlook the difference among future states, committing to specific answers even when the queried facts are inherently volatile. To capture this challenge, we introduce ChronoRegime, a future-oriented temporal reasoning task that requires models to determine whether historical temporal evidence justifies commitment to a future answer. Furthermore, we propose Confidence-Aware Temporal Reasoning (CTR), a framework that estimates future predictability from temporal dynamics and regulates answer commitment accordingly. Rather than performing unconditional forecasting, CTR commits only when the reconstructed evidence supports the target future state. Across multiple LLMs, CTR improves strict overall accuracy by 6.7 percentage points and reduces hallucination rates by 18.4 percentage points on average over the plain QA baseline. These results demonstrate that explicit predictability assessment is an effective mechanism for safer and more reliable temporal reasoning under future uncertainty.

articles.text:
Welcome to the first Cloud CISO Perspectives for October 2026. Today, Stephanie Kiel explains the latest on our approach to post-quantum cryptography, and shares a new tool to help CISOs and executives prepare their organizations for PQC.
As with all Cloud CISO Perspectives, the contents of this newsletter are posted to the Google Cloud blog. If you’re reading this on the website and you’d like to receive the email version, you can subscribe here.

New Gemini Notebook can help CISOs and policymakers prepare for PQC
By Stephanie Kiel, Head of Cloud Security Policy, Government Affairs and Public Policy, Google Cloud
Stephanie Kiel, Head of Cloud Security Policy, Government Affairs and Public Policy, Google Cloud
Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is one of the most urgent security shifts of the decade — and one of the easiest to tune out. For security leaders and policymakers, the research is dense, scattered across papers and engineering blogs, and can be challenging to turn into action.
To help, we're launching Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography, a public Gemini Notebook that brings Google's PQC research, engineering blogs, and migration guidance together in one place. Ask it questions, listen to an audio overview, or test yourself with flashcards, and quickly get up to speed on the quantum threat.
Why PQC matters now
Quantum computing is rapidly moving from theory to reality. Our Willow chip and Quantum Echoes algorithm mark substantial progress, and Google research estimates that breaking ECDLP-256 and RSA-2048 encryption — the public-key cryptography schemes protecting much of our online data — would require around 500,000 and 1 million imperfect quantum computer components (noisy qubits), respectively.
To help, we're launching Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography, a public Gemini Notebook that brings Google's PQC research, engineering blogs, and migration guidance together in one place.
This research has consequences now. It indicates that today’s online security is more vulnerable to future quantum computers than previously thought.
In Store Now, Decrypt Later attacks, adversaries may steal encrypted data now and wait to decrypt it once a sufficiently powerful quantum computer exists. Data that we’ve long considered sensitive — health records, financial data, intellectual property, and government secrets — is already at risk.
With continued advances in architecture, quantum algorithms, and quantum error correction shrinking future quantum hardware requirements, waiting to upgrade our digital locks is not a viable option. To help organizations stay ahead of the curve, Google has published a migration timeline noting our plans to transition to PQC by 2029, and we urge others to consider the same.
As the technology advances, policymakers should consider urging critical infrastructure owners and operators to recognize condensed timelines, and build PQC readiness into existing risk mitigation plans. We also recommend governments engage with global counterparts to promote a harmonized approach to standards development, and include technical and security experts in the building of policy and regulatory requirements focused on quantum safety.
Google's PQC expertise, in one notebook
The Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography notebook turns years of Google expertise into an interactive primer that anyone can use. It's built on curated Google sources covering the quantum era, quantum computing breakthroughs like Willow, Quantum Echoes, and surface code error suppression, industry PQC standards, Google's own deployments, and the latest research.
In the Gemini Notebook, you can:
Get answers grounded in Google's sources.
Listen to a podcast-style audio overview.
Test your PQC knowledge with flashcards.
Explore an interactive visual diagram of the quantum threat.
Read a concise briefing document.
Try these prompts
To get started, here are a few questions to ask the notebook:
For CISOs: "What should a CISO prioritize in the first 90 days of a PQC migration?"
For anyone new to PQC: "Explain store-now-decrypt-later in plain terms."
For developers: "How does hybrid ML-KEM key exchange work in Chrome?"
As with all generative AI, the notebook can make mistakes, so check its responses against the linked sources.
What's at stake
Previous cryptographic migrations, such as moving from SHA-1 or upgrading TLS, have taken a decade or more. Waiting for the availability of a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer before beginning the migration journey represents a significant security risk given the importance of public-key cryptography for securing digital essentials like web traffic, software updates, digital identities, and signatures.
For CISOs, we recommend that you start by:
Understanding where vulnerable cryptography lives in your organization.
Identifying and prioritizing data and systems most at risk from quantum threats, and developing a plan for addressing these risks.
Anticipate system-wide effects that PQC migration could have.
Building crypto-agility into your security plans, using learnings from past experiences like Heartbleed.
Additional detail on these recommendations is available in our previous blog post.
For the broader security community, the transition only succeeds if this knowledge is accessible to everyone — not just organizations with dedicated cryptography teams.
How Google is putting PQC into practice
We’ve been deploying PQC for years. Highlights include:
Hybrid Kyber/ML-KEM key exchange protecting Chrome traffic
PQC in Android
Quantum-safe digital signatures in Cloud KMS
PQC for Google's internal communications
Wiz PQC readiness scanner across code, cloud, and runtime
We also co-founded the Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance at the Linux Foundation with industry leaders including Amazon Web Services, Cisco, IBM, and NVIDIA to support open-source tools like Open Quantum Safe.
Build a PQC notebook for your own team
Here’s how you can create a resource similar to our PQC Gemini Notebook, specific to your organization’s needs:
Curate trusted sources. Start with a focused set of authoritative research, standards, and guidance.
Write neutral prompts. Keep instructions factual so outputs stay grounded in your sources.
Add AI disclaimers and a welcome note. Tell readers what the notebook covers and remind them that AI can make mistakes.
Review all output with human oversight. Have experts check every artifact before you share it.
Start preparing today
The quantum transition has already started, but preparing your organization doesn't have to begin with a 100-page whitepaper. Start by understanding the threat, then assess your cryptographic inventory and build a migration roadmap.
You can get started with the Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography Gemini Notebook and share it with your team today. To learn more about Google Cloud’s approach to PQC, check out our dedicated Google Cloud PQC Resource Hub.

articles.title: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam

Nearly eight years after Epic took on Steam with its own Game Store and launcher, the Fortnite maker is deploying a new tool to give it an edge over Valve: vibe coding.
In announcing the new publicly available "Preview" build of its Epic Games Launcher, Epic writes that "programming is hard. So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look." And while that might sound a little tongue-in-cheek, Epic Games Store General Manager and VP Martin Keely told PC Gamer that the team "started from scratch" and used AI as "a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously." The goal, Keely said, was to "look at functionality that existed [in the current Epic Games Launcher] and [say] we want to replicate that, but not the code itself."
Speaking to IGN, Keely clarified that using AI to code the new Launcher "made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well."

articles.title: Who Receives Respect? A Counterfactual Benchmark for Honorific Allocation Bias in Bengali
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14769v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Bengali has no grammatical gender, but honorificity is obligatory: every third-person reference must choose ordinary or respectful register. English has no such signal, so the system must choose a level of deference that the source never specified. We use this property to measure how large language models (LLMs) allocate respect in English--Bengali translation. Our evaluation set contains 2{,}016 sentences across 72 occupations. Each appears in seven sentence frames under four pronoun conditions. Masculine and feminine versions differ by one word, forming counterfactual pairs. We report a single Honorific Bias Score (HBS) for each model on a 0--100 scale, covering both the gender and occupation axes. A lower score means that respect is allocated more evenly. For the occupation analysis, we compute each occupation's honorific rate across the seven no-pronoun sentence frames. The standard deviation of these 72 occupation-level rates ranges from 17.2 to 35.5 percentage points across models, showing substantial variation in how honorifics are allocated across occupations. Occupation is associated with 3.2\% to 51.5\% of the variance in register choice, compared with at most 1.2\% for gender. Gender effects are much smaller overall: only two of the nine models show significant directional gender gaps, and they favor opposite genders. HBS ranges from 19.9 to 70.1 across the nine models, showing substantial variation in how evenly the models allocate respect.

articles.title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14635v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.

articles.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
articles.text:
A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment.
Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases.
Cutting proteins
The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid. This is critical for building up the long chains found in proteins. (The amino acids also have side chains with distinctive chemistry, which gives a backbone specific properties.)

Software partners including ABA Technology, Akila, Galene AI, Honeywell Technologies, K2K, Linker Vision, Milestone, Onetera, ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services.

Building the AI Infrastructure for European Cities
For European cities, scaling from pilots to everyday operations requires infrastructure that can process local data, customize models and run AI agents.

EY and Accenture provide the integration and operational expertise to connect applications with city systems. Their work helps cities build repeatable deployment blueprints that they can adapt across departments and expand as local needs grow.

articles.title: 马斯克自曝：过去一年里，我大概经历了六次“赛博精神病”
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，当地时间 14 日，据《商业内幕》报道，马斯克出席上周六的 X Takeover 活动，在访谈中大谈 AI 的神奇之处，随后却少有地谈起自己的感受：“我有点‘赛博精神错乱’，其实可能还挺严重。”
他称，过去一年里，自己大概经历了六次“AI / SI 精神错乱”（IT之家注：SI 指的是美国总统特朗普将人工智能改称的“超级智能”）。
“AI 精神错乱”并非正式医学术语，也没有公认的定义。通常指人们反复使用 AI 后，原有的妄想变得更加严重。
这个词也曾被用来讽刺对 AI 深信不疑、使用起来近乎痴迷的科技圈人士。一些精神科医生则认为，如果使用 AI 加重了原有的心理脆弱性，也可能引发精神健康问题。
后来，一些科技圈人士反倒把“AI 精神错乱”当成值得骄傲的标签。今年 5 月的一场聚会上，参加者甚至齐声喊起口号：“一、二、三，AI 精神错乱！”
风险投资家马克 · 安德森大力推崇“AI 精神错乱即服务”（AIPAAS）的说法，还把与之相反的状态称为“AI 自我安慰”（AI cope）。
Y Combinator CEO 陈嘉兴（Garry Tan）今年 3 月也曾开玩笑说：“我有‘赛博精神错乱’，但我觉得，我认识的 CEO 里有三分之一也这样。”
最近，帕兰提尔 CTO 希亚姆 · 桑卡尔举了一个例子：一些 AI 研究人员相信，AI 将来能够治愈癌症，因此开始吸烟。他认为，这正是硅谷“集体精神错乱”的体现。
马斯克所说的 AI“精神错乱”，则指自己相信 AI 能够理解美。他直言：“你会觉得，‘天哪，AI 居然也懂审美？简直不可思议。’”
值得一提的是，此次并非马斯克首次提到该概念。今年 4 月，安德森曾在 X 上发帖，称人有三种状态：“AI 狂喜、AI 精神错乱，以及 AI 精神错乱的精神错乱。”马斯克只回复了一个词：“对。”

articles.title: 科技大佬拼酒量：马斯克豪饮 3 品脱夺魁，扎克伯格喝黑啤面露难色成全网热梗
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，科技媒体 metro 昨日（10 月 14 日）发布博文，报道称在互联网世界中，科技大佬们的明争暗斗从不局限于商场与企业实力，甚至连杯中的啤酒都能成为新的战场。
欧洲最具影响力的每日直播科技节目 @etnshow 昨日（10 月 14 日）在 X 平台发布推文，统计了《The Cheeky Pint》播客节目中受邀嘉宾的酒量，并推出了“Cheeky Pint 饮酒排行榜”（The Cheeky Pint Benchmark）。
IT之家注：《The Cheeky Pint》是近年来在科技界与创投圈迅速走红的一档高端科技深度访谈播客节目。该节目打破了传统商业采访的严肃与刻板，以其独特的“酒馆社交”风格著称。
节目的固定录制场景是一个充满爱尔兰风味的传统小酒馆。每一期节目，Stripe 联合创始人约翰 · 科里森（John Collison）都会邀请科技创始人或行业领袖“边喝啤酒边聊天（over a pint）”。
Meta 首席执行官扎克伯格与公司首席 AI 官汪滔（Alexandr Wang）一同做客该节目，扎克伯格甚至特意从都柏林空运了一整桶正宗的爱尔兰健力士（Guinness）黑啤。
在扎克伯格喝下第一口黑啤后，他的面部表情管理似乎瞬间“失控”。网民们迅速捕捉到了他眉头紧锁、近乎痛苦的 wince（龇牙咧嘴）表情，该片段在各大社交平台疯狂流传。有网友调侃道：“他仿佛在试图咀嚼那口啤酒”，还有人开玩笑称“这可能是他这辈子遇到过最艰难的挑战”。
面对排山倒海的恶搞，扎克伯格本人通过其社交账号（@finkd）冷冷地幽默回应了一句：“那只是我的日常表情（that's just my face）”。
就在扎克伯格的“饮酒囧态”引发互联网狂欢之际，该节目的数据统计随之出炉。播客团队的内部人员强制让实习生看完了往期所有节目，精准计算出了各位科技巨头在录制时的真实饮酒量，并推出了“Cheeky Pint 饮酒排行榜”。
在这份涵盖了 38 位科技巨头的榜单中，全球首富埃隆 · 马斯克在做客该节目时轻松灌下整整 3 品脱（约 1.7 升）的健力士黑啤，展现出惊人的豪饮实力。
尽管第一口喝得极其痛苦，但扎克伯格最终还是硬着头皮喝掉了 1 又 1/6 品脱（约 663 毫升），虽然比不过马斯克，但依然排到了前十，甚至击败了 Anthropic 的创始人达里奥 · 阿莫代（Dario Amodei）。

articles.title: Seamless Deployment of Machine Learning Inference at the Far Edge: An Empirical AWS IoT Greengrass Architecture for Industrial Predictive Maintenance
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.14815v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Industrial IoT sensors produce continuous, high-volume data streams that predictive maintenance needs to analyse in real time. Cloud-centric architectures send all raw telemetry to central servers, which costs latency, bandwidth and resilience. This paper presents a hybrid cloud-edge architecture for manufacturing predictive maintenance built on AWS IoT Core and AWS IoT Greengrass v2, with local machine learning inference at the edge and selective cloud synchronization. We deploy two configurations on real AWS infrastructure and compare them: a cloud-only baseline (Configuration A) and the proposed hybrid edge architecture (Configuration B). We measure end-to-end inference latency, bandwidth consumption and inference accuracy. Configuration B cuts cloud-bound bandwidth by 86.8% (63.6 KB to 7.2 KB per 200-reading window) and decision latency by 256x (23.1 ms cloud round trip to 0.09 ms local inference). At the edge, with no cloud involvement, it keeps an anomaly-class F1 score of 0.84 and 91% recall. The evaluation also instruments system uptime and Stream Manager queuing under cloud disconnection; the quantitative disconnection experiment is left as planned work. Our review of the literature points to four gaps that this work addresses: the lack of empirically validated Greengrass v2 deployments for predictive maintenance, unquantified bandwidth savings from selective edge synchronization, unmeasured resilience under cloud disconnection, and the open MLOps feedback loop at the edge.

articles.title: OpenAI’s Math Breakthroughs Rattle Cryptography Leaders
articles.text:
OpenAI’s release last Tuesday of more than 300 math results it says an internal model solved has sparked concern among some of the world’s leading cryptographers, or experts in encoding information to keep it private and secure. They worry that AI’s continued math advances could find new algorithms that make our current methods of protecting information on encrypted services, from online payments to messaging platforms like WhatsApp, easier to crack.
The basis for modern internet security is the assumption that some math operations are easy to do, such as a process of encoding using a number known as the public key. But they are hard to undo, or decode, without knowing a specific number, called the private key. This assumption of difficulty is the foundation of secure communication over the internet, which has helped enable e-commerce, cryptocurrencies and digital accounts.
AI models from OpenAI and others, which have been solving problems that have stumped math experts for decades, have raised the prospect that powerful AI systems could find ways to solve those problems without that key.
“I am anticipating a vast change in mathematics, cryptanalysis included,” said Whitfield Diffie, who helped invent public key cryptography in 1976 with the Diffie-Hellman key exchange algorithm, in an email to me.
“I don’t know the timescale. A year is probably too soon; five may not be,” said Diffie, now a consulting scholar at the Stanford Center for International Security and Cooperation.

articles.title: 苹果首款折叠屏iPhone Duo跑分出炉：A20 Pro性能看齐iPhone 18 Pro
articles.text:
快科技10月15日消息，苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo将于10月16日开启预购，10月23日正式发售，新机的性能表现也提前揭晓。
日前，iPhone Duo现身Geekbench 7跑分平台，单核成绩3986分，多核成绩11067分，整体表现与iPhone 18 Pro系列基本处于同一水平。
根据Geekbench数据库信息，此次参与测试的设备型号为iPhone19,4，运行iOS 27.1系统，搭载苹果最新A20 Pro芯片。
该芯片采用6核心CPU设计，包括2颗性能核心和4颗能效核心，最高主频达到4.93GHz，与iPhone 18 Pro系列保持一致。
内存方面，Geekbench识别到的容量为11.30GB，对应实际12GB运行内存。
据了解，iPhone Duo与iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max均搭载A20 Pro芯片，采用台积电2nm工艺打造。
苹果表示，A20 Pro相比上一代A19 Pro，CPU性能最高提升20%，GPU性能最高提升40%。
从目前曝光的跑分来看，iPhone Duo的成绩虽然略低于部分iPhone 18 Pro系列机型，但整体差距不大。
需要注意的是，目前仅有一组iPhone Duo跑分成绩曝光，单次测试结果存在一定波动，尚不能代表新机的最终性能表现。
此外，由于iPhone Duo采用折叠屏设计，内部空间和散热结构与传统直板旗舰有所不同，其持续性能释放仍有待实际测试。
作为苹果首款折叠屏手机，iPhone Duo采用横向内折设计，配备5.4英寸外屏和7.6英寸内屏，国行售价15999元起。

articles.title: 麦肯锡面试新花样：先和 AI 客户对线十分钟
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据华尔街日报报道，想在麦肯锡拿到工作？你或许先要成功和人工智能虚拟对手对线。
这家顶尖咨询公司将于今年秋季调整部分初级咨询岗位候选人的面试流程，新增一类客户模拟环节。该环节旨在测试应聘者的临场应变能力，以及和麦肯锡客户沟通的水平，其中部分客户会更加刨根问底、难以应对。
尽管全程都是模拟场景，但这场时长约十分钟的 AI 对话，会安排在麦肯锡真实的办公室内进行，合伙人或面试考官会在现场观察候选人的表现。
麦肯锡的合伙人表示，这套 AI 工具不会自行对候选人的表现打分或给出评价。这个虚拟形象学习了多种客户性格类型，例如那种像学者一样、希望深入理解公司方案建议的客户。
参与该试点项目设计、任职于麦肯锡达拉斯办公室的合伙人萨利姆 · 扎法尔（Saleem Zafar）称，该工具并非用来模拟情绪失控的客户，或是刻意设置陷阱提问的客户，它的目标是还原麦肯锡顾问日常工作中八成会遇到的场景。
扎法尔说：“我重点观察的是：你有没有捕捉到对方话语里的关键信息？有没有据此做出回应？还是直接忽略了这些内容？会不会固守自己预设的思路，强行把答案灌给对方。我们要看的，是你面对不断变化的信息时如何反应。”
今年秋季，麦肯锡正在北美部分办公室，对申请商业分析师岗位的本科生测试这套虚拟对手面试系统，预计将有数百名候选人参与。如果试点效果良好，公司计划明年把它推广到其他岗位。
各行各业的企业都在调整招聘方式，以此适应人工智能时代，更好发挥这项技术的能力。部分雇主新增 AI 筛选工具，还有企业在招聘流程中引入作弊检测软件。
长期以来，想要拿到麦肯锡的 offer，需要经历多轮繁琐考核。候选人一般要和合伙人及其他面试官面谈，之后参与案例分析挑战，现场解决问题。
如今，案例挑战结束后，候选人还要在笔记本电脑上和 AI 虚拟形象对话。
麦肯锡负责全球招聘工作的联合负责人布莱尔 · 西塞尔（Blair Ciesil）表示：“借助这种方式，我们可以考察候选人与人打交道的综合素养，而不受提前准备的影响。有些候选人会准备一套反复演练好的陈述。不是说这些经历不够出色，但这会让面试官很难看清候选人内在的真实特质。”
扎法尔举了一个假设案例：某座城市聘请麦肯锡，调研新体育场馆的选址。在这个场景里，AI 虚拟形象就扮演市长，对顾问提出的方案进行质询。
他说：“市长会有一些自己十分看重的诉求，希望听取你的建议。但当你阐述方案时，她可能会提出更多顾虑，或是补充更多背景信息。”
IT之家注意到，也有不少企业不愿在招聘中使用人工智能，担心产生偏见，或是违反不断更新的招聘领域 AI 相关法规。麦肯锡的合伙人表示，这套 AI 工具意在提升招聘流程的公平性，因为在角色扮演环节里，不同人类面试官的严苛程度存在差异。
扎法尔称，在招聘工作中，公司要预判“这个人未来能不能胜任工作”。这套新工具，就是为了帮助面试官更好地看清：“这个人本质是什么样的？他真实的一面是怎样的？”
